title: Atlas Documents are supreme over Synome Documents, and Synome commentary has no governance meaning
content:
A.1.3.1.4 states the conflict rule and then goes further: "In any case of conflict between an Atlas Document and a Synome Document, the Atlas Document takes precedence. Synome Documents may include explanations or commentary, but such content is informative only and has no governance significance. The governance meaning of any principle, rule, or process is established solely in the Atlas Documents."

The second and third sentences are the interesting ones, because they anticipate a specific failure mode. In practice, the authoritative description of a system's behaviour drifts toward wherever the operative detail lives — comments in code, docstrings, spec annotations — because that is what implementers read. Left unaddressed, the Synome's commentary would gradually become the real rulebook while the Atlas became aspirational.

Declaring commentary non-operative by fiat closes that path. It also means a discrepancy between the Atlas and the Synome is unambiguously a **Synome defect**, never an interpretive question: there is nothing to weigh. A.1.3.2's conforming-update obligation follows directly — when an Atlas change makes the Synome non-conforming, the Synome must move.

This mirrors the treatment of Translation Documents (A.1.2.2.2.23), which also lose to the canonical original on any discrepancy. The Atlas repeatedly resolves multi-representation problems by nominating one authoritative artefact and demoting all mirrors to informative, rather than by building machinery to reconcile them. It is a consistent and deliberately unsophisticated strategy: fewer things to interpret means fewer places for drift to enter.
description: A.1.3.1.4 makes governance meaning established solely in Atlas text, so explanations inside code or specifications are informative only — code cannot become the rule by accident.
